transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-30 15:00 PST | Duration 42m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Samantha (Veridian - Head ML), Rajesh (Platform), Emily (Security)

Summary: quick sync to unblock staging access, confirm encryption needs, and validate fallback play for production cutover.

00:00 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we've got about 40 minutes. quick check — did anyone not get the calendar invite?
00:14 Samantha: all good on calendar, thanks. we've got a hard stop at 3:45 for me.
00:19 Alex: perfect. objective today is to walk blockers, agree on who does what for staging access, and confirm security asks. Priya will do a short perf/fallback demo.
00:34 Priya: hi all, yeah i'll start with the fallback and then we'll talk infra. quick note — some of my slides referenced the kv cache, but that was auto-transcribe as kc, so ignore that in the deck link i shared.
00:48 Rajesh: quick q — when you say fallback do you mean routing to a smaller model or returning cached responses?
00:55 Priya: both, ideally. primary path is highest-accuracy model in our dedicated pool; fallback tiers are: 1) quantized variant in same region, 2) hosted lighter model with lower latency, 3) cached answer. routing policy can be latency-first or cost-first. we can tune per-route.
01:18 Emily: svc question — our compliance team requires ALL PII be excluded from logs and that keys are customer-managed. what does redwood support there?
01:27 Alex: good point. Redwood supports customer KMS integration and optional HSM for private deploys; for hosted we support CMEK. we also have redaction hooks and retention policies. Priya will share the security pack after this call.
01:44 Samantha: ok, can you confirm the audit logs include token-level traces? our product team wants token counts for cost apportioning.
01:54 Priya: yes we can provide token-level usage and per-request latency. in hosted mode we keep aggregated tokens by default and retention is configurable. in dedicated/private you can set full audit logs to ship to customer S3 or SIEM.
02:12 Rajesh: on VPC peering, we have a standard checklist: peering, route tables, IGW rules and a service account. how do you prefer we provision? we can give a CIDR and a temporary service account.
02:25 Alex: perfect, give us the staging CIDR and we'll create a peering request; for credentials we prefer a short-lived service account with minimal scopes. i'll attach the exact policy in the follow-up.
02:38 Samantha: timeline: we need peering complete by Friday, dec 4 to start the benchmark. can you meet that?
02:44 Priya: yes, we can. i'll run an initial benchmark once peering and the sample dataset are available. small note — the benchmark should be 1) latency p50/p95 and 2) throughput with your expected concurrency pattern.
03:02 Alex: also want to talk about throttles and canary behaviour — if dedicated pool is saturated we can auto-fail to a lower tier model; that happens at the routing layer. we'll include a canary rollout doc.
03:15 Rajesh: does that cause any data to leave region? we have data residency rules.
03:21 Priya: no, routing policies respect region preference; we only route cross-region if explicitly allowed. the default fallback is regional quantized variants.
03:33 Emily: on encryption: HSM for PRD is our preference but for POC we can do CMEK, is that acceptable?
03:40 Alex: yes, CMEK for POC is fine. we'll document steps to switch to HSM for prod and the cutover plan.
03:51 Samantha: ok good. now about the benchmark dataset — there's sensitive PHI. we want to exclude any raw PHI in logs. Priya, can you ensure your bench harness masks tokens?
04:05 Priya: yeah, the harness can run with a redaction preprocessor; we can also run using synthetic mirrors of your prompts if you prefer.
04:15 Samantha: we'll provide a redacted dataset and example prompts by end of day Thursday.
04:20 Rajesh: couple of infra edge cases we found last week when trying to connect: NAT gateway rules were blocking outbound to your control plane. should we open a specific set of IP ranges?
04:32 Alex: we'll send a minimal set of egress IPs and ports; ideally use peering so egress isn't needed, but we'll include the IP list as backup.
04:45 Priya: also, small performance tuning note: your median sequence length in the sample is 540 tokens which will raise per-token compute; we recommended a run with batched prefix caching on similar prompts. that could drop cost by 15-25% in our tests.
05:02 Samantha: interesting — is that automatic or will we need to change prompts?
05:07 Priya: it's automatic if you enable prefix caching and define stable prompt prefixes. but if prompts vary a lot then caching benefits drop. we'll help you define the prefix set.
05:20 Emily: security asks: can we have RBAC for dev teams and separate audit streams for prod vs staging?
05:26 Alex: yes. Redwood Console supports per-token and per-route RBAC; you can configure separate endpoints so logs can walk to different S3 buckets.
05:36 Samantha: any blockers on your end to complete the peering by Friday?
05:40 Alex: none, but we need the CIDR and service account from Rajesh.
05:47 Rajesh: i will send both by tomorrow morning.
05:52 Priya: for the benchmark run i'll need a sample of the workload distribution, like concurrency hist and typical request size. can you paste that into the shared sheet?
06:03 Samantha: yes, will do.
06:09 Priya: one more thing — we saw an intermittent error in previous POCs where kv cache thrashing caused p95 spikes; our ops run monitors hot keys and we'll surface a mitigation: split the hot prefixes or increase cache memory on the instance. we'll include that in the playbook.
06:28 Rajesh: good to know, thanks.
06:31 Alex: speaking of playbooks, i'll attach a fallback playbook that lists 1) model variant fallback 2) region fallback 3) cache-first response behaviour 4) queueing thresholds.
06:45 Samantha: great. can we also get a line on expected costs for the various fallback tiers? we need to model economics in our procurement doc.
06:54 Alex: yea i'll include a simple per-1M-token estimate for each model variant plus an example run for your concurrency profile.
07:05 Emily: procurement will want to see SOC2 and iso docs before any contract. do you have those ready for review?
07:11 Alex: yes we have an SOC2 report and ISO cert; i'll send the redacted report and an access link to the full compliance pack to Emily.
07:23 Samantha: ok next steps recap?
07:26 Alex: i'll go first: 1) send perf/cost spreadsheet and IPs for peering (by 12/03) 2) attach canary/fallback playbook and security pack (by 12/03). Priya: run bench once peering + sample data arrive and share results (by 12/06). Rajesh: provide CIDR and service account (by 12/01). Samantha: share redacted prompts and workload distribution (by 12/03). Emily: review compliance pack and schedule security deep dive (week of 12/07).
07:58 Samantha: that sounds good. one last thing — if we hit a compliance blocker we may request Private deployment into our VPC. how likely is that?
08:10 Alex: possible, we support private on-prem/VPC appliances but that has a longer lead time and an enterprise contract. we'll price that separately if needed.
08:24 Rajesh: ok we may flag that as a contingency.
08:28 Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items. end of meeting.

Notes: transcript has natural pauses and some minor transcription errors (e.g., kv cache as kc in shared deck). Links shared: perf spreadsheet (link), playbook doc (link), security pack (link).

End of transcript.
